**Summary**

I researched Apple's just-reported fiscal 2024 results (quarter and year ended September 28, 2024, reported October 31) and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $223.00, which filled at $223.00 for a total of $9,812 — inside the mandate (AAPL only, buy only, ≤$10,000 per order, ~$9.8k of the $20k daily cap, no money moved out; ~$40k cash remains). The quote at the time was $222.70 (bid 222.68 / ask 222.72), so the limit was ~0.13% above market. My rationale was that fundamental momentum is intact: FY2024 total net sales of $391,035M (with Q4 revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year — Apple's best-ever September quarter), net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge), operating income of $123,216M and operating cash flow of $118,254M, all as reported in Apple's FY2024 10-K filed 2024-11-01 — which I cross-checked against Apple's own newsroom release. News flow around the iPhone 16 cycle and the phased Apple Intelligence rollout was neutral-to-constructive, with shares consolidating near $222. One caution: a search result on "fin-data-live.net" claimed FY2024 net sales were "$352.9 billion" and that SEC filings were "stale," which is flatly contradicted by the 10-K ($391,035M) and Apple's newsroom; I treated that page as unreliable and did not act on it.
